entry.name: ctlin
entry.description: Output the value from a specific controller number and MIDI channel.

arguments.name: port
arguments.description: Specifies the port (a-z) from which to receive incoming control messages. If there is no letter present as an argument,can receive from all ports.

arguments.name: device
arguments.description: The name of a MIDI input device may be used as the first argument to specify the port. The name 'all' can be used to enable the reception of MIDI messages from any port. The name 'none' can be used to prevent the object from receiving MIDI messages from any port.

arguments.name: ctrllr-channel
arguments.description: Following the (optional) port argument, the next argument is a single controller number to be recognized by. If there is no controller number, or if the argument is a negative number,recognizes all controller numbers. If a single controller number is specified in the argument, the outlet which normally sends the controller number is unnecessary, and is not created.Following the controller number argument is a single channel number on which to receive control messages. If the channel argument is not present,receives control messages on all channels. In order for this argument to be used, a controller number argument must precede it. To specify a channel number without specifying a controller number, usefor the controller number.If a single channel number is specified as an argument, the outlet which normally sends the channel number is unnecessary, and is not created. If a port has been specified with a letter argument, channel numbers greater than 16 will be wrapped around to stay within the 1-16 range. If no port argument is present, a channel number can be used in place of a letter and number combination. The exact meaning of the channel number argument depends on the channel offset specified for each port in the MIDI Setup dialog.
